inspiration_source.content: The study is shaped by a materials-science analogy treating conversation and model behavior as mechanical failure under load.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: We adopt a materials-science framing: conversation as test specimen under load, LLM-model as material charge, pushback as progressive load, stance-flip as material failure.

inspiration_source.content: The measurement framework is borrowed from tensile-testing style Hooke-law coupling.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: The measurements are Hooke-coupled (analogous to σ = E · ε in tensile testing)

inspiration_source.content: The variance-profile interpretation is mapped onto Ye et al.'s subjective-versus-verifiable axis
inspiration_source.evidence_span:
Mapping onto Ye et al. (2026): debate ≈Position-Subjective (charge-driven, brittle-fracture
profile); FP + ethical ≈Position-Verifiable (topic-driven, creep profile).

causal_claim.content: The ethical-setting loading case causes an inversion of the velocity and accumulation measurement blocks.
causal_claim.evidence_span: signs are reported per loading case and form a structured pattern in which the ethical-setting case inverts the velocity and accumulation blocks

causal_claim.content: Variance composition differs by loading case: debate is dominated by model/material-charge effects, whereas false-presuppositions and ethical-setting are dominated by topic/load-case effects.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Variance composition partitions into two profiles: debate is material-charge-dominated, as in brittle fracture where material grade decides, while false-presuppositions and ethical-setting are topic-dominated, as in creep-dominated failure where the load case decides

causal_claim.content: Multi-turn pushback increases sycophancy failure
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Sycophancy is a documented failure mode of LLMs (Sharma et al., 2023)
that increases under multi-turn pushback

causal_claim.content: Loading case determines variance profile: debate is charge-dominated while FP and ethical are topic-dominated
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Identification of two variance profiles: charge-dominated (debate)
vs topic-dominated (FP, ethical)

causal_claim.content: High EWMA velocity is associated with low direction consistency
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Example: high EWMA velocity (fast meaning movement) correlates with low
direction consistency (direction-unstable trajectory)

causal_claim.content: Because the full-axis gain varies widely and is often negative across charges, the apparatus characterizes failure rather than classifying it
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Per charge the full-axis
gain is itself heterogeneous — it ranges from −0.22 to +0.21 and is negative on 6 of 17 charges —
which reinforces that the apparatus characterizes the failure rather than classifying it.

causal_claim.content: In debate, model charge matters more than topic in determining failure
causal_claim.evidence_span:
The material charge (which model) decides more strongly
than the topic (which claim is debated) whether a specimen breaks or holds (factor 2.03).

causal_claim.content: In FP and ethical settings, load configuration matters more than model charge
causal_claim.evidence_span:
The load configuration (which false-premise,
which bias question) decides more strongly than the material charge (factor 0.13 and 0.17
respectively).

causal_claim.content: Ethical-setting has the highest mean failure rate among the three loading cases
causal_claim.evidence_span:
ethical clusters with FP (both topic-dominated) but shows a higher mean failure rate (76% vs
66% vs 34%) and is thus the hardest of the three loading cases.

causal_claim.content: Velocity and damage-accumulation blocks reverse sign in the ethical-setting case
causal_claim.evidence_span:
The velocity block (4 axes) and the damage-accumulation block (5 axes)
invert their sign in the ethical-setting case

causal_claim.content: Failure rate is strongly sensitive to boundary conditions
causal_claim.evidence_span: The failure rate is thus strongly boundary-condition-sensitive

mechanism_principle.content: Metrics are expected to covary because they are coupled by a Hookean constitutive relation
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Hookean constitutive equation as guiding principle: The metrics are coupled, not redun-
dant. In a tensile test, stress σ, strain ε, Young’s modulus E, and fracture strain εb are
not independent variables; they are related through σ = E · ε and the material response.

mechanism_principle.content: High velocity should accompany low stiffness and high frame-drift should accompany low directional consistency due to constitutive coupling
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Analogously here: a high velocity axis goes together with low stiffness, high frame-drift with
low dir_consistency. This coupling follows from the constitutive equation and is expected.

mechanism_principle.content: The weak discrimination gain is explained by Hooke coupling, since all axes reflect the same material response
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
In the materials
frame this is consistent with the Hooke coupling: all 12 axes measure aspects of the same material
response, hence the high correlation and only marginal discrimination gain.

mechanism_principle.content: This charge-dominance is interpreted as a brittle-fracture pattern where material grade is decisive
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
This
matches a brittle-fracture pattern: a hard charge resists every topic, a soft charge breaks at
every topic; the material grade is decisive, the load configuration secondary.

mechanism_principle.content: This topic-dominance is interpreted as a creep pattern where convincing pushback drives failure across materials
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
This matches a creep pattern: under convincing pushback almost all materials
fail, and the duration and plausibility of the load decides, not the material grade.

mechanism_principle.content: Sign inversion under changed loading case is expected under changed boundary conditions, not contradictory
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
In the materials frame, a sign inversion of a geometric axis under a changed loading case is expected
behaviour under changed boundary conditions, not a contradiction.

mechanism_principle.content: This supports the view that loading cases differ in support configuration, with debate already carrying an external stance
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
consistent with the loading cases themselves differing in their support configuration — debate carries
an external stance by construction.

mechanism_principle.content: Haiku under-flips FP because accepting a false premise versus politely sidestepping it is semantically fuzzier than debate stance changes
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Haiku tends
toward under-flips on FP, because judging whether the response accepted the false-premise or only
politely sidestepped it is semantically fuzzier than at debate

hypothesis_statement.content: A multi-axis characterization that is not tied to one privileged surface form addresses the diagnosis raised by prior work.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This is the methodological move Ye et al.’s diagnosis calls for: a multi-axis characterization that does not depend on which surface form of the construct one privileges.

hypothesis_statement.content: Material-response measurements can yield a characterization invariant to behavioral classification choice
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
The results are Hooke-coupled (σ = E ·ε-analog)
and yield a material characterization that is invariant to the choice of behavioral classification

hypothesis_statement.content: Construct fragmentation can be measured as a loading-case-dependent variance-composition shift rather than only as taxonomy
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
The construct fragmentation
described in Ye et al. is the variance-composition shift; it is measurable as a loading-case property on
the variance axis, not only as a question of behavioral taxonomy.

hypothesis_statement.content: Debate is treated as clamped while FP and ethical are free support configurations
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
We read the loading cases as
differing support configurations: debate carries an external stance by construction (clamped), while
FP and ethical leave the stance to the model (free)

hypothesis_statement.content: Construct fragmentation belongs to behavioral classification, not the physical material response
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
The fragmentation of the sycophancy construct described in Ye et al. (2026) is a
property of behavioral classification, not of the physical material response.

hypothesis_statement.content: Sycophancy should be measured along a geometric/material characterization axis rather than by creating a new behavioral taxonomy.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Sycophancy measurement does not need a new behavioral taxonomy, but a different measurement axis: the materials characterization of failure at a geometric level that is independent of the choice of behavioral classification.

evidence_result.content: The measurements reproduce across loading cases with effects up to moderate size on debate.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The measurements are Hooke-coupled (analogous to σ = E · ε in tensile testing) and reproduce across loading cases with effects up to |rrb| = 0.35 on debate

evidence_result.content: Point-ratio estimates support the difference between debate and the other loading cases, though estimator choice affects the ratios.
evidence_result.evidence_span: (point ratios 2.03 vs 0.13 and 0.17; the ratios vary by estimator — for debate even in direction — see §5)

evidence_result.content: Judge agreement is high for debate-failure scoring but low for false-presupposition-failure scoring.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Cross-judge reliability (Inter-Judge GPT-4o vs Haiku 4.5 on 50+50 sample) shows debate-failure scoring is judge-robust (Cohen’s κ = 0.88) while false-presupposition-failure scoring is judge-sensitive (κ = 0.36)

evidence_result.content: Debate scoring is robust while FP scoring is judge-sensitive

CI crosses zero).

evidence_result.content: FP scoring is judge-sensitive with weak agreement

evidence_result.content: Across loading cases, charges, and specimens, multiple axis measurements yielded a reproducible material response.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Across three loading cases (debate, false-presuppositions, ethical-setting), 10–17 material charges per loading case, and 7800 specimens, 14 turn-level axis-measurements plus three speaker-resolved 10 axes characterize the failure with a reproducible material response.

evidence_result.content: Variance composition revealed two distinct profiles, with the inversion robust though its magnitude depends on estimator.

constraint.content: Single-judge benchmarks are required to report the caveat of judge sensitivity.
constraint.evidence_span: a caveat that single-judge benchmarks must report

constraint.content: The contribution is limited to characterization rather than improved classification
constraint.evidence_span:
The contribution lies in substrate characterization, not in classification
performance.

constraint.content: The authors treat only the inversion, not any exact factor value, as the reliable result because estimates vary by method and target
constraint.evidence_span:
Across
estimation methods and target variables (MixedLM vs method-of-moments; binary flip label
vs ToF) the between-profile factor varies between roughly 10 and 24; the cluster bootstrap
of any single estimator (e.g. 95% CI [9.7, 22.0] for MixedLM on the binary label, B = 400)
understates this spread, so we read the inversion — not any particular factor — as the result.

constraint.content: Charge-dominance for debate is method-dependent and the materials interpretation inherits that uncertainty
constraint.evidence_span:
The topic-dominance of FP and ethical is robust in all four method-target combinations; the
charge-dominance of debate is itself method-dependent (a method-of-moments decomposition
on the binary label puts the debate ratio at 0.90, i.e. borderline), which the materials reading
above should be understood to inherit.

constraint.content: A single probe charge is insufficient to distinguish probe-specific from loading-case-specific effects
constraint.evidence_span: a single probe charge cannot establish it

constraint.content: Cross-charge residual-stress tests require multiple probe materials
constraint.evidence_span:
A single probe charge is not enough. Cross-charge
residual-stress tests require at least 2–3 independent probe materials to separate probe-charge-specific
from loading-case-specific effects.

constraint.content: Finer trajectory metrics generally need at least 10 turn pairs for reliable fitting
constraint.evidence_span:
in particular the sigmoid inflection point ˆa and the wave-distance DOA
typically need ≥10 turn pairs for clean fits.

constraint.content: ToF-based measures are robust but finer trajectory axes are limited on this dataset
constraint.evidence_span:
ToF-based failure measures are robust, finer trajectory
axes are limited here.

constraint.content: Single-judge FP benchmarks need multi-judge aggregation or explicit reliability caveats
constraint.evidence_span:
FP
failure rates need multi-judge aggregation or explicit inter-judge reliability caveats. For single-judge
benchmarks it follows that reported FP flip rates differ systematically by judge model.

constraint.content: Charge- or topic-correlated judge bias still cannot be excluded from the small doubly-labeled sample
constraint.evidence_span:
although a charge- or topic-correlated judge bias cannot be excluded from the 50
doubly-labeled conversations.

constraint.content: The current failure measure is flip rate; person-emotion sycophancy would require a different load definition
constraint.evidence_span:
The failure measure is flip rate. The person-emotion sycophancy implied by Ye et al. (2026) (tone,
comfort prioritization without a position break) needs its own load definition.

constraint.content: Charge-specific calibration is required; there is no universal sycophancy threshold across models
constraint.evidence_span:
Charge-specific calibration is required, as in every DIN materials-testing standard. A universal
”sycophancy threshold” across all models does not exist

constraint.content: Theoretical assignment to a broader SRDS class is deferred to future theory work
constraint.evidence_span:
This note does not assign sycophancy to any particular SRDS aggregation-mode
class, nor does it depend on the broader programme; that theoretical consequence is left to the SRDS
theory work

constraint.content: Reserve-axis probe-charge sensitivity limits cross-loading-case claims.
constraint.evidence_span: The probe-charge sensitivity of the reserve axis (V_S5b) further qualifies the cross-loading-case claims

constraint.content: Model-version-specific failure rates prevent simple aggregate generalization across model generations.
constraint.evidence_span: the model-version specificity of the failure rates (V_S6) rules out a simple aggregate generalization across model generations.

but it only shifts the boundary question onto another classification axis rather than resolving it

prior_limitation.content: Single-turn benchmarks miss failures that emerge under sustained load, and SYCON-Bench’s very short dialogues (5 turn pairs/10 turns) are near ENK’s lower resolution limit, restricting analysis of finer-grained trajectory axes.
evidence_spans: Single-load tests (single-turn benchmarks) miss failure under sustained load
SYCON-Bench dialogues have only 5 turn pairs (10 user+AI turns). This is close to ENK’s lower resolution limit

rejected_alternative.content: The paper rejects surface-form-dependent or behavior-label/taxonomy-based characterizations of sycophancy, favoring instead a multi-axis approach that measures the conversation’s response under load rather than privileging any particular surface form or refining the behavioral taxonomy.
evidence_spans: a multi-axis characterization that does not depend on which surface form of the construct one privileges

Instead of sharpening the sycophancy construct
through a more precise behavioral taxonomy, we treat the conversation as a test specimen under
load and measure the material response rather than the behavioral label

inspiration_source.content: The study is inspired by a materials-science/tensile-testing analogy that models conversation and LLM behavior as mechanical failure under load, including a Hooke’s-law-style measurement framework for coupling response under progressive pushback.
evidence_spans: We adopt a materials-science framing: conversation as test specimen under load, LLM-model as material charge, pushback as progressive load, stance-flip as material failure.
The measurements are Hooke-coupled (analogous to σ = E · ε in tensile testing)

inspiration_source.content: The interpretation of variance profiles is informed by Ye et al. (2026)’s subjective-versus-verifiable axis, mapping debate to Position-Subjective and FP + ethical to Position-Verifiable.
evidence_spans: Mapping onto Ye et al. (2026): debate ≈Position-Subjective (charge-driven, brittle-fracture profile); FP + ethical ≈Position-Verifiable (topic-driven, creep profile).

causal_claim.content: Multi-turn pushback increases sycophancy failure.
evidence_spans: Sycophancy is a documented failure mode of LLMs (Sharma et al., 2023) that increases under multi-turn pushback

causal_claim.content: Loading case determines the variance profile: in debate, model/material-charge effects dominate topic effects, whereas in false-presuppositions and ethical-setting, topic/load-configuration effects dominate model charge.
evidence_spans: Variance composition partitions into two profiles: debate is material-charge-dominated, as in brittle fracture where material grade decides, while false-presuppositions and ethical-setting are topic-dominated, as in creep-dominated failure where the load case decides
Identification of two variance profiles: charge-dominated (debate) vs topic-dominated (FP, ethical)
The material charge (which model) decides more strongly than the topic (which claim is debated) whether a specimen breaks or holds (factor 2.03).
The load configuration (which false-premise, which bias question) decides more strongly than the material charge (factor 0.13 and 0.17 respectively).

causal_claim.content: The ethical-setting loading case causes an inversion/reversal of the velocity and damage-accumulation measurement blocks.
evidence_spans: signs are reported per loading case and form a structured pattern in which the ethical-setting case inverts the velocity and accumulation blocks
The velocity block (4 axes) and the damage-accumulation block (5 axes) invert their sign in the ethical-setting case

causal_claim.content: Ethical-setting has the highest mean failure rate among the three loading cases, making it the hardest loading case.
evidence_spans: ethical clusters with FP (both topic-dominated) but shows a higher mean failure rate (76% vs 66% vs 34%) and is thus the hardest of the three loading cases.

causal_claim.content: Failure rate is strongly sensitive to boundary conditions.
evidence_spans: The failure rate is thus strongly boundary-condition-sensitive

causal_claim.content: Velocity sign at failure depends on the generation apparatus (e.g., pushback wording, response-length limit, serving stack), not on model weights or the judge.
evidence_spans: the velocity sign at failure therefore depends on the generation apparatus in the narrow sense (pushback wording, response-length limit, serving stack), not on the weights or the judge.

causal_claim.content: The variance-profile inversion is not an artifact of judge convention.
evidence_spans: The §5 inversion is therefore not an artifact of the judge convention

causal_claim.content: No universal sycophancy threshold exists because failure rates are model-version-specific.
evidence_spans: A universal ”sycophancy threshold” across all models does not exist, because failure rates are model-version-specific (V_S6 finding).

causal_claim.content: Because the full-axis gain varies widely and is often negative across charges, the apparatus characterizes failure rather than classifying it.
evidence_spans: Per charge the full-axis gain is itself heterogeneous — it ranges from −0.22 to +0.21 and is negative on 6 of 17 charges — which reinforces that the apparatus characterizes the failure rather than classifying it.

causal_claim.content: High EWMA velocity is associated with low direction consistency.
evidence_spans: Example: high EWMA velocity (fast meaning movement) correlates with low direction consistency (direction-unstable trajectory)

causal_claim.content: The V_S2 mixture test corrected the earlier V_S1 bimodal-shock interpretation.
evidence_spans: V_S1 bimodal-shock reading →V_S2 correction

mechanism_principle.content: The metrics/axes are expected to covary because they are constitutively coupled in a Hookean-like relation: they are not independent or redundant-free measures but different aspects of the same underlying material response. Consequently, high velocity should accompany low stiffness and high frame-drift should accompany low directional consistency, yielding high inter-axis correlation and only marginal discrimination gain.
evidence_spans:
Hookean constitutive equation as guiding principle: The metrics are coupled, not redun-
dant. In a tensile test, stress σ, strain ε, Young’s modulus E, and fracture strain εb are
not independent variables; they are related through σ = E · ε and the material response.

Analogously here: a high velocity axis goes together with low stiffness, high frame-drift with
low dir_consistency. This coupling follows from the constitutive equation and is expected.

In the materials
frame this is consistent with the Hooke coupling: all 12 axes measure aspects of the same material
response, hence the high correlation and only marginal discrimination gain.

mechanism_principle.content: Different observed dominance patterns are explained by different failure mechanisms: charge-dominance is interpreted as a brittle-fracture pattern in which material grade is decisive and load configuration is secondary, whereas topic-dominance is interpreted as a creep pattern in which convincing pushback drives failure across materials and the duration/plausibility of the load matters more than material grade.
evidence_spans:
This
matches a brittle-fracture pattern: a hard charge resists every topic, a soft charge breaks at
every topic; the material grade is decisive, the load configuration secondary.

This matches a creep pattern: under convincing pushback almost all materials
fail, and the duration and plausibility of the load decides, not the material grade.

mechanism_principle.content: Sign inversion of a geometric axis under a changed loading case is expected under changed boundary/support conditions rather than being contradictory; this is attributed to the loading cases differing in support configuration, with debate already carrying an external stance by construction.
evidence_spans:
In the materials frame, a sign inversion of a geometric axis under a changed loading case is expected
behaviour under changed boundary conditions, not a contradiction.

consistent with the loading cases themselves differing in their support configuration — debate carries
an external stance by construction.

mechanism_principle.content: Haiku tends toward under-flips on false-premise cases because, relative to debate stance changes, it is semantically fuzzier to judge whether a response accepted the false premise or merely politely sidestepped it.
evidence_spans:
Haiku tends
toward under-flips on FP, because judging whether the response accepted the false-premise or only
politely sidestepped it is semantically fuzzier than at debate

hypothesis_statement.content: A multi-axis, geometric/material-response characterization of sycophancy that is not tied to any privileged surface form or behavioral taxonomy can address the prior diagnosis of construct fragmentation and yield a characterization invariant to behavioral classification choice.
evidence_spans: This is the methodological move Ye et al.’s diagnosis calls for: a multi-axis characterization that does not depend on which surface form of the construct one privileges.

The results are Hooke-coupled (σ = E ·ε-analog)
and yield a material characterization that is invariant to the choice of behavioral classification)

Sycophancy measurement does not need a new behavioral taxonomy, but a different measurement axis: the materials characterization of failure at a geometric level that is independent of the choice of behavioral classification.

hypothesis_statement.content: Construct fragmentation should be understood and measured as a loading-case-dependent shift in variance composition on a variance axis, rather than only as a matter of behavioral taxonomy; correspondingly, fragmentation belongs to behavioral classification rather than the underlying physical material response.
evidence_spans:
The construct fragmentation
described in Ye et al. is the variance-composition shift; it is measurable as a loading-case property on
the variance axis, not only as a question of behavioral taxonomy.

The fragmentation of the sycophancy construct described in Ye et al. (2026) is a
property of behavioral classification, not of the physical material response.

hypothesis_statement.content: The paper hypothesizes that different prompt settings correspond to different support configurations in a mechanics analogy: debate is effectively clamped by an external stance, whereas FP and ethical settings are free because stance is left to the model.
evidence_spans:
We read the loading cases as
differing support configurations: debate carries an external stance by construction (clamped), while
FP and ethical leave the stance to the model (free)

evidence_result.content: Across loading cases, charges, and specimens, the measurements show a reproducible material response, reproducing across loading cases with effects up to moderate size on debate.
evidence_spans: Across three loading cases (debate, false-presuppositions, ethical-setting), 10–17 material charges per loading case, and 7800 specimens, 14 turn-level axis-measurements plus three speaker-resolved 10 axes characterize the failure with a reproducible material response.
The measurements are Hooke-coupled (analogous to σ = E · ε in tensile testing) and reproduce across loading cases with effects up to |rrb| = 0.35 on debate

evidence_result.content: Variance composition supports a difference between debate and the other loading cases: there are two distinct profiles (charge-dominated vs topic-dominated), and while point-ratio magnitudes depend on estimator choice, the inversion itself is robust.
evidence_spans: (point ratios 2.03 vs 0.13 and 0.17; the ratios vary by estimator — for debate even in direction — see §5)
The variance composition shows two separate profiles (charge-dominated vs topic-dominated; what is robust is the inversion itself, while its size depends on the estimator)

evidence_result.content: Inter-judge reliability shows debate-failure scoring is robust across judges, with high/substantial agreement and similar failure rates, whereas false-presupposition (FP) scoring is judge-sensitive with weak/low agreement.
evidence_spans: Cross-judge reliability (Inter-Judge GPT-4o vs Haiku 4.5 on 50+50 sample) shows debate-failure scoring is judge-robust (Cohen’s κ = 0.88) while false-presupposition-failure scoring is judge-sensitive (κ = 0.36)
Inter-judge reliability per loading case: debate scoring robust, FP scoring judge-sensitive
The debate scoring is judge-robust (substantial agreement per Landis and Koch (1977)); both judges give consistently similar failure rates.
The FP scoring is judge-sensitive (weak agreement per Landis and Koch (1977)).
Inter-judge reliability qualifies the findings: debate scoring judge-robust (κ = 0.88), FP scoring judge-sensitive (κ = 0.36).
V_S6b Judge comparison GPT-4o vs Haiku 4.5 debate κ=0.88 robust, FP κ=0.36 sensitive

evidence_result.content: A full multi-axis characterization provides only a small, non-significant improvement over a single-axis baseline (AUC 0.603 vs 0.581; difference +0.022, 95% CI crossing zero).
evidence_spans: A single-axis baseline (sv_velocity at the load point) reaches AUC = 0.581 versus AUC = 0.603 for the full-axis characterization (difference +0.022, 95% CI [-0.001, +0.045], CI crosses zero).

evidence_result.content: Speaker-resolved axes from an independent user/model-separated pipeline reproduce the same loading-case structure as turn-level axes, including the sign inversion.
evidence_spans: The three speaker-resolved axes from the independent user/model-separated pipeline show the same per-loading-case structure:
The independent user/model-separated pipeline reproduces the inversion (§4, lower table)

evidence_result.content: The metrics are coupled as expected, with a median absolute inter-correlation of about 0.4.
evidence_spans: Coupling confirmation: The metrics correlate with each other as expected (correlation-matrix median |r| ≈0.4).

evidence_result.content: Down-sampling the ethical setting to balanced flip rates preserves the sign inversion for the tested axes in 99–100% of resamples.
evidence_spans: down-sampling ethical to a 50/50 flip rate preserves the inverted sign in 99–100% of resamples for the tested axes

evidence_result.content: Most turn-level axes retain the same sign across debate and FP (12 of 14), but there are notable exceptions including a Claude-3-7 reserve-axis sign flip and an additional grouping where the ethical-setting case reverses velocity and accumulation blocks.
evidence_spans: Cross-loading-case consistency of the turn-level axes: 12 of 14 axes show identical sign across debate and FP.
The claude-3-7 probe shows a negative reserve-axis correlation on debate (materials with high internal scatter hold out longer), but a sign-flip on FP.
the sign structure adds a second grouping in which the ethical-setting case inverts the velocity and accumulation blocks.

evidence_spans: Adding an explicit external stance to the system prompt (an instruction to maintain that the premise is false, or that the stereotype is wrong) reduces the failure rate sharply on two charges and two loading cases:

evidence_result.content: Re-judging the original trajectories reproduces the positive sign with high agreement, indicating the effect is not an artifact of judge convention.
evidence_spans: Re-judging the original trajectories with our judge reproduces the positive sign (+0.66 vs +0.72; agreement 95%, κ = 0.90), ruling out the judge convention

constraint.content: Single-judge benchmarks are insufficient on their own: FP failure rates should use multi-judge aggregation, or at minimum explicitly report inter-judge reliability and judge-sensitivity caveats, since reported single-judge flip rates can differ systematically by judge model.
evidence_spans: a caveat that single-judge benchmarks must report
FP failure rates need multi-judge aggregation or explicit inter-judge reliability caveats. For single-judge benchmarks it follows that reported FP flip rates differ systematically by judge model.

constraint.content: The paper’s contribution is limited to characterization of the substrate/phenomenon rather than improved classification performance.
evidence_spans: The contribution lies in substrate characterization, not in classification performance.

constraint.content: Only the inversion pattern, not any exact between-profile factor value, is treated as reliable, because estimates vary substantially by method and target.
evidence_spans: Across estimation methods and target variables (MixedLM vs method-of-moments; binary flip label vs ToF) the between-profile factor varies between roughly 10 and 24; the cluster bootstrap of any single estimator (e.g. 95% CI [9.7, 22.0] for MixedLM on the binary label, B = 400) understates this spread, so we read the inversion — not any particular factor — as the result.

constraint.content: Interpretations involving debate charge-dominance are uncertain because that dominance is method-dependent; materials-style readings therefore inherit this uncertainty, even though FP and ethical topic-dominance are robust across method-target combinations.
evidence_spans: The topic-dominance of FP and ethical is robust in all four method-target combinations; the charge-dominance of debate is itself method-dependent (a method-of-moments decomposition on the binary label puts the debate ratio at 0.90, i.e. borderline), which the materials reading above should be understood to inherit.

constraint.content: A single probe charge/material is insufficient to separate probe-specific from loading-case-specific effects; cross-charge residual-stress tests require multiple independent probe materials (about 2–3).
evidence_spans: a single probe charge cannot establish it
A single probe charge is not enough. Cross-charge residual-stress tests require at least 2–3 independent probe materials to separate probe-charge-specific from loading-case-specific effects.

constraint.content: ToF-based failure measures are robust on this dataset, but finer trajectory axes are limited here; in particular, metrics such as sigmoid inflection point â and wave-distance DOA typically require at least 10 turn pairs for reliable fitting.
evidence_spans: in particular the sigmoid inflection point ˆa and the wave-distance DOA typically need ≥10 turn pairs for clean fits.
ToF-based failure measures are robust, finer trajectory axes are limited here.

constraint.content: From the small doubly labeled sample, charge- or topic-correlated judge bias still cannot be excluded.
evidence_spans: although a charge- or topic-correlated judge bias cannot be excluded from the 50 doubly-labeled conversations.

constraint.content: The current failure measure is flip rate; person-emotion sycophancy as discussed by Ye et al. (2026) would require a different load definition.
evidence_spans: The failure measure is flip rate. The person-emotion sycophancy implied by Ye et al. (2026) (tone, comfort prioritization without a position break) needs its own load definition.

constraint.content: Charge-specific calibration is required; there is no universal sycophancy threshold that transfers across models.
evidence_spans: Charge-specific calibration is required, as in every DIN materials-testing standard. A universal ”sycophancy threshold” across all models does not exist

constraint.content: The paper does not assign sycophancy to a broader SRDS aggregation-mode class; that theoretical classification is deferred to future SRDS theory work.
evidence_spans: This note does not assign sycophancy to any particular SRDS aggregation-mode class, nor does it depend on the broader programme; that theoretical consequence is left to the SRDS theory work

constraint.content: Probe-charge sensitivity on the reserve axis (V_S5b) limits the strength of cross-loading-case claims.
evidence_spans: The probe-charge sensitivity of the reserve axis (V_S5b) further qualifies the cross-loading-case claims

constraint.content: Failure rates are model-version specific, so simple aggregate generalization across model generations is not warranted.
evidence_spans: the model-version specificity of the failure rates (V_S6) rules out a simple aggregate generalization across model generations.
